```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,dev='png')
out <- params$directory
```

## Reading this report

Sampling reliability, posterior uncertainty, directional support and predictive fit answer different questions. Beta diagnostics are the primary assessment. Passing screens is reassuring diagnostic evidence, not proof of convergence. In-sample predictive performance cannot override poor coefficient convergence.

Rank-normalised split/folded R-hat > 1.01, bulk or tail ESS < 100 × chains, and mean MCSE/posterior SD > 0.05 are separate flags. Undefined diagnostics are **cannot assess**. Every saved draw is retained with chain identity; second-half summaries are sensitivity checks only.

Posterior intervals describe conditional uncertainty. Support is max(P(Beta > 0), P(Beta < 0)); wrong-sign probability is one minus support (including ties at zero conservatively). Zero observed wrong-sign draws do not imply certainty. Support does not measure ecological importance. No Holm correction or draw selection is applied. Support summaries for flagged or unassessable coefficients are unreliable; selection counts use passing coefficients only.

Spatial correlations describe overlap, not coefficient bias. Saved factors have arbitrary sign and basis; combined Eta × Lambda effects are invariant under compensating factor transformations. Spatial correlations have their own convergence diagnostics. Projected space and Beta use the saved X scale, including intercepts; within-chain correlations describe compensation. Each spatial level is assessed separately; its sum with Beta excludes other random levels. Rank deficient designs cannot identify individual projected coefficients.

Group summaries are descriptive, with species and coefficient denominators. Broad uncertainty denotes the upper quartile of interval width **within predictor**; intercepts remain separate. Migration values preserve fitted coding. Missing traits are shown as missing. Prevalence uses observed responses as denominator, and includes rare and near-ubiquitous species.

```{r notes, results='asis'}
cat(params$notes,'\n\n')
if(file.exists(file.path(out,'provenance.R'))) cat('Input fingerprint, sampling, scaling, thresholds and versions: [provenance.R](provenance.R); [session info](session-info.txt).\n')
```

```{r output-helpers, include=FALSE}
show_csv <- function(files) for(f in files) {
 cat('\n\n### ',sub('\\.csv$','',basename(f)),'\n\n',sep='')
 cat('[Download full CSV](',basename(f),')\n\n',sep='')
 d<-read.csv(f,check.names=FALSE)
 if(basename(f)=='model-comparison.csv') for(i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {cat('[',d$model[i],'](',d$report[i],')',sep='');if('report_pdf' %in% names(d)) cat(' | [PDF](',d$report_pdf[i],')',sep='');cat('  \n')}
 cat('Rows: ',nrow(d),'. First ',min(if(knitr::is_latex_output()) 10 else 15,nrow(d)),' shown.\n\n<div class="table-scroll">\n\n',sep='')
 if(knitr::is_latex_output()) {
   preferred<-c('species','predictor','model','group','family','threshold','status','rhat','ess_bulk','ess_tail','mcse_sd_ratio','median','n_coefficients','n_species','fraction_flagged','selected','expected_wrong_sign')
   cols<-head(unique(c(intersect(preferred,names(d)),names(d))),7)
   dd<-head(d[,cols,drop=FALSE],10)
   names(dd)<-gsub('_',' ',names(dd))
   for(v in names(dd)) if(is.character(dd[[v]])) dd[[v]]<-ifelse(nchar(dd[[v]])>35,paste0(substr(dd[[v]],1,32),'...'),dd[[v]])
   cat('\\begingroup\\scriptsize\n')
   print(knitr::kable(dd,digits=3,format='latex',booktabs=FALSE,longtable=FALSE,row.names=FALSE))
   cat('\n\\endgroup\n')
 } else print(knitr::kable(head(d,15),digits=4))
 cat('\n\n</div>\n\n')
}
show_png <- function(files) for(f in files) {
 if(knitr::is_latex_output()) cat('\\clearpage\n')
 cat('\n\n### ',sub('\\.png$','',basename(f)),'\n\n',sep='')
 if(knitr::is_latex_output()) {
  cat('\\begin{center}\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.80\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{',normalizePath(f),'}\n\\end{center}\n',sep='')
 } else cat('![',basename(f),'](',normalizePath(f),'){width=100%}\n',sep='')
}
show_section <- function(pattern) {
 csv<-list.files(out,pattern='\\.csv$',full.names=TRUE)
 png<-list.files(out,pattern='\\.png$',full.names=TRUE)
 if(knitr::is_latex_output()) png<-png[!grepl('^beta-(rhat|ess_bulk|ess_tail)-(intercepts|slopes)',basename(png))] else png<-png[!grepl('^print-heatmap-',basename(png))]
 show_csv(csv[grepl(pattern,basename(csv))]);show_png(png[grepl(pattern,basename(png))])
}
```

## Beta convergence: primary assessment

Heatmaps include every coefficient; intercepts are separate. Grey means undefined. The second-half check does not alter the primary draws. Detailed chain plots use the deterministic union of the worst five R-hats and lowest five bulk and tail ESS, plus up to three passing coefficients selected in species/predictor order.

```{r beta, results='asis'}
show_section('^(beta-|diagnostic-|selected-|model-comparison|print-heatmap-)')
```

<details><summary>Selected coefficient trace, rank, density and autocorrelation plots</summary>

```{r chain-plots, results='asis'}
show_section('^coefficient-')
```

</details>

## Where problems and uncertainty concentrate

Species, guild and migration summaries use environmental slopes only. Predictor summaries include intercepts as a separate group. All coefficients remain in denominators; counts of cannot-assess coefficients are reported separately.

```{r concentration, results='asis'}
show_section('^(concentration-|uncertainty-|rhat-vs-|width-vs-)')
```

## Spatial overlap and chain differences

Combined effects are the main spatial results. Each correlation is computed within a saved draw across the specified cells. Combined-chain tables show posterior distributions by chain; their R-hat and ESS are in the combined-correlation tables. Saved-field plots are conditional on the saved factor basis. If there are no spatial random levels this section is inapplicable, as recorded above.

```{r spatial, results='asis'}
show_section('^(spatial-|shared-cell-)')
```

## Directional support and multiplicity

Families are all environmental slopes within each model, and intercepts separately. The comparison report also pools the selected models' slopes. Expected wrong-sign counts sum posterior wrong-sign probabilities among selected passing coefficients; proportions divide by selected count. These are conditional posterior quantities, without a Holm adjustment.

```{r support, results='asis'}
show_section('^directional-')
```

## In-sample predictive fit

Hmsc metrics use all saved draws. Prediction arrays are not exported. Good in-sample performance cannot establish coefficient convergence or out-of-sample accuracy.

```{r fit, results='asis'}
show_section('^(in-sample-|fit-)')
```

```{r supplement, results='asis'}
show_section('^(gamma-|rho-)')
```
